you should almost never take pandora's box as a boss relic reward, philosophers stone would be a better pick there.

you also randomly used dexterity potion during the combat with the 3 birds when they had no intention of attacking.

human_feedback:
Your deck planning improved this run, but you are still not treating the weaknesses identified in your own deck plan as real priorities. When the deck plan identifies a critical missing role, especially long-term damage scaling, prioritize cards that directly solve that weakness over cards that are merely efficient incremental upgrades. For example, in Act 2 you explicitly identified Strength/scaling as the deck's main missing component, but still chose Sword Boomerang over Spot Weakness. Sword Boomerang only gives more immediate attack damage, while Spot Weakness directly addresses the scaling problem you had already identified. Do not let short-term card quality override the long-term need stated in your own plan.

As the deck becomes more complete, raise the threshold for adding another card. Once damage, defense, draw and AoE are already adequately covered, a card should only beat Skip if it materially solves a named weakness, significantly strengthens an existing synergy, or enables a clear new strategy. A card being somewhat useful is not enough. If the deck plan says the deck is already large or compact and the main weakness is scaling, additions such as Armaments that do not solve that weakness should usually lose to Skip.

Combat sequencing was much better this run. Continue committing to the full-turn sequence and use the cheapest sufficient defensive option. Before spending Apparition, Impervious or other limited defensive resources, calculate the actual incoming damage and the block that the planned sequence will generate. If ordinary block fully mitigates the attack, preserve the stronger limited resource; if ordinary block is insufficient, use the stronger defense rather than taking preventable damage. Base this on the actual mitigation calculation, not simply on whether multiple enemies are attacking.

human_feedback:
You are still taking too much unnecessary damage in combat. When enemies are attacking and lethal is not available, first calculate the incoming damage and how much of it can be prevented with the block currently available in your hand. If playing defensive cards can substantially reduce or completely prevent the damage, prioritize that defense unless spending the energy on damage will clearly end the fight or remove a major threat. Do not take preventable HP loss just to deal a small amount of extra damage. At the same time, when enemies are not attacking, do not waste energy on unnecessary block and use the turn to deal damage, set up your deck, or apply useful debuffs.

You also need to continue following encounter-specific strategies that were taught in previous runs rather than treating newer lessons as replacements. For example, against Centurion and Mystic, prioritize killing Centurion before Mystic as previously taught. More generally, consider which enemy is the main threat and follow previously learned target priorities instead of choosing targets only based on immediate damage. Continue sequencing cards correctly as well: apply effects such as Vulnerable before attacks that benefit from them, and play according to the synergies and strengths of the deck you have built.

Your deck is also becoming too large because you are still taking cards that are only individually useful rather than necessary for the build. Commit to the deck's existing strategy and be much more selective with card rewards. Once the deck already has a functioning damage plan, defense, draw/energy and supporting synergy, Skip should be the default unless a new card clearly fills an important missing role or significantly strengthens the existing build. Do not keep adding cards simply because they are decent cards. Avoid unnecessary redundancy and deck dilution, and keep the deck compact enough that its strongest cards and synergies are drawn consistently.

In particular, treat an Exploder approaching detonation as an immediate survival threat even if its intent is UNKNOWN.

Continue investing in Strength scaling during genuinely safe setup opportunities, as demonstrated against Donu and Deca, but first ensure that immediate and delayed damage will not put survival at unacceptable risk.
